newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma wheat harvest begins on limited acreage.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma wheat harvest begins on limited acreage.

text.p: Harvesting began on a very limited segment of Oklahoma's winter wheat crop during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday in its weekly crop progress report.

Wheat harvest began in a few sandy areas of eastern Tillman County before showers stopped combines on Thursday night, the report said. "Rains were particularly welcome in the eastern third of Oklahoma," it said.
The state's wheat was rated 12 percent very poor, 14 poor, 38 fair and 36 good. A week ago, wheat rated 11 percent very poor, 16 poor, 36 fair, 36 good and one excellent.
Sixty-one percent of the wheat crop had reached the soft dough stage, versus 79 last year and 72 on average.
Corn was 99 percent up-to-stand, against 96 average. Soybeans were 60 percent planted, ahead of 45 percent average.
Sorghum acreage was 15 percent planted, versus 44 percent last year and 43 percent on average.
Pasture and range conditions improved over the previous week and were rated nil very poor, two percent poor, 19 percent fair, 66 percent good and 13 percent excellent.
